2025-01.daily_overview: A normal workday. In the morning, after ward rounds, I processed the long-term medication orders for several patients with chronic conditions. In the afternoon, I attended a departmental professional discussion. In the evening, I went to the supermarket for groceries, and at night I video-called my mother and relaxed with music and journaling.

events.name: Ward rounds and patient communication.
events.description: At 8 a.m., Yu Xiaowen attended the department morning meeting on time, then joined Li Wei on ward rounds. The several elderly patients under her care were in stable condition. During the rounds, she also took time to chat for ten minutes with a coronary heart disease patient who was anxious, soothing their emotions.

events.name: Adjust standing medical orders
events.description: After ward rounds, she returned to the office, turned on her computer, reviewed the long-term medications of several patients with diabetes and hypertension, adjusted the doses of glucose-lowering drugs based on the latest lab reports, and notified the nurses to carry out the changes.

events.name: Midday reading of medical journals
events.description: During the lunch period, Yu Xiaowen ate quickly in the cafeteria, then went to the sofa in the doctors' lounge, opened the latest issue of the Chinese Journal of Internal Medicine, read a review article about new lipid-lowering drugs, and took notes.

events.name: Participating in departmental case discussion
events.description: At 2:30 pm, the department held its usual weekly Friday difficult-case discussion. Today's case was a fever of unknown origin. The doctors each shared their views, and Yu Xiaowen also raised her hand to speak, offering her opinion from a rheumatology and immunology perspective, which was affirmed by Dr. Liu Qiang.

events.name: Supermarket shopping and running into a neighbor
events.description: On her way home from work, Yu Xiaowen turned into the Dennis supermarket on Jingsan Road, pushed a shopping cart, and picked out chicken breast, broccoli, apples, and yogurt. In the fresh food section, she ran into an aunt who lives in the same building. They chatted briefly about the community's new property management rules, and Yu Xiaowen helped the aunt carry a bag of rice downstairs.

events.name: Video-called her mother to catch up on family matters
events.description: After dinner, Yu Xiaowen sat on the sofa and called her mother, Li Xiuying, on WeChat video. On the screen, her mother was mending clothes. She talked about how Dad had recently become quite obsessed with chess, and asked Xiaowen whether she was eating well. Xiaowen told her about the pottery class. Her mother said in surprise, 'My daughter has such clever hands,' and urged her to keep warm and not catch cold.

events.name: Evening music and diary time
events.description: After hanging up the video call, Yu Xiaowen played Mozart's piano concerto on her Bluetooth speaker, then took out her diary and used a fountain pen to write down the day's experiences and reading insights. At 9:30, after washing up, she lay in bed and fell asleep peacefully after listening to two pieces of music.

2025-01.daily_overview: After her morning run, Yu Xiaowen attended her second basic pottery class. Under the guidance of Teacher Zheng, she mastered advanced hand-building techniques and made a small teacup. After class, she had a lively conversation with a new friend, Su Ya, and the two agreed to collaborate on making tea sets, full of creative enthusiasm.

events.name: Early morning jog by the river.
events.description: At 7 a.m., as dawn was just breaking, Yu Xiaowen put on her sportswear and jogged along Jingsan Road to the Dongfeng Canal riverside greenway. Although the temperature was near freezing, her body warmed up quickly once she started running. After running about 2.5 kilometers, she stopped to stretch by the river, breathed in the crisp air, and returned home feeling refreshed.

events.name: Pottery class: advanced hand-building and teacup making.
events.description: At 9 a.m., she arrived at the studio on time. Zheng Guodong, the instructor, first commented on everyone's small bowls from the previous class, pointing out the common problem of overly thick bottoms, and then taught new techniques: how to use fingers to evenly close in the cup rim and use a scraper to smooth the surface. At the pottery wheel, Yu Xiaowen took a fist-sized lump of clay, carefully shaped it into a teacup with a slightly inward-curving rim and moderately thin walls. Although the handle was installed a bit crooked, the overall result pleased her.

events.name: In-depth conversation at the café after class
events.description: After the class ended, Yu Xiaowen and Su Ya hit it off immediately and walked to the nearby Summer Aroma cafe. They each ordered a latte and sat on the sofa by the window. Su Ya opened her phone gallery and shared teapots and flower containers she had made before, each exquisite and adorable. Xiaowen also showed the small teacup she had just made that day, and the two discussed the flow experience that pottery brought, with laughter filling the air.

events.name: Agreed to collaborate on teaware creation
events.description: The more they talked, the more they hit it off. Su Ya suggested, 'Why don't we make a tea set together?' Yu Xiaowen's eyes lit up and she agreed immediately. They initially decided to design a tea set in a simple Chinese style, comprising one teapot and four cups. Su Ya would be responsible for the teapot body and handle, and Xiaowen for the four cups. They also agreed to each draw a design sketch before the next class. This agreement made Yu Xiaowen feel that she had found a pottery partner.

events.name: Afternoon home review and seasonal tidying
events.description: After returning home in the afternoon, Yu Xiaowen made a cup of honey water and sat at her desk, flipping through the electrocardiogram chapter of Practical Internal Medicine while sketching a teacup design on draft paper. Later, she spent half an hour organizing the thick sweaters and thin coats in her wardrobe, preparing for the coming deep winter.

events.name: Evening manual therapy consolidation practice
events.description: After dinner, she cleaned off the coffee table, spread out old newspapers, took out the remaining clay, and repeatedly practiced kneading clay and coiling clay strips. She recorded her practice video and sent it to the small WeChat group with Su Ya, where the two commented on each other's shortcomings in a lively atmosphere.

2025-01.daily_overview: On a leisurely Sunday, after morning stretching, Yu Xiaowen drove to the bookstore to buy a favorite novel, enjoying a quiet time of coffee and reading. In the evening, she practiced pottery techniques at home and connected with Su Ya via video to practice together.

events.name: Morning stretching and household chores
events.description: On Sunday morning at 7:30, Yu Xiaowen woke up naturally without setting an alarm. She spread out her yoga mat in the living room, followed a video for a 15-minute gentle stretch, and then made a cup of oatmeal with boiling water. After breakfast, she started the washing machine to wash the sheets and vacuumed the entire apartment floor.

events.name: Drove to the Book Center
events.description: At 1:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowen put on her beige down jacket and drove west along Jinshui Road. There were not many cars on the road, and about 15 minutes later she arrived at Zhengzhou Book Center. She parked in the underground parking lot, took the elevator upstairs, and walked straight to the literature section.

events.name: Book shopping and coffee reading time
events.description: At the bestseller display, she was attracted by the cover of Keigo Higashino's Miracles of the Namiya General Store. After flipping through a few pages, she decided to buy it. Then she went to the coffee corner on the second floor of the bookstore, ordered a hot latte, and sat by the window. Snowflakes were falling outside the window. Holding the hot coffee, she became immersed in the wonderful story of the Namiya General Store and read for an hour and a half without noticing, until her phone alarm reminded her it was time to go home.

events.name: Repair the loose shoe heel.
events.description: After leaving the bookstore, she noticed that the heel of her left ankle boot was a bit loose, so she found a shoe repair shop nearby and spent 10 minutes having the heel glued. The craftsman worked quickly. She paid by scanning a QR code and continued driving home.

events.name: Return home to tidy up and try new dishes
events.description: At 4:30 p.m., she paid, left with the new books, and drove back along the same route. After getting home, she put the new books on the bedside table and spread the clean sheets on the bed. At dinner, she tried making a low-fat version of sweet and sour pork tenderloin in the air fryer. It didn't look great, but it tasted good.

events.name: Evening independent pottery practice
events.description: After dinner, Yu Xiaowen continued practicing kneading clay on the coffee table. This time she tried coiling clay strips into a small plate. She opened a WeChat video call and connected with Su Ya. The two chatted while working on their crafts. Su Ya shared a sketch of a tea set she had drawn, and Xiaowen showed off the cup handle shaped like a zodiac rat that she was trying to make. They agreed to finalize their designs before Thursday's class.

2025-01.daily_overview: On a workday, Yu Xiaowen volunteered during ward rounds to take over a complex patient with multiple systemic diseases, and was permitted by her supervising teacher. After that, she devoted herself wholeheartedly to studying the case, consulting literature late into the night.

events.name: Monday morning meeting and case handover
events.description: At 8 a.m., Yu Xiaowen attended the department's regular handover meeting as usual. The night-shift doctor highlighted a 72-year-old male patient with type 2 diabetes, chronic renal failure (CKD stage 4), and concurrent heart failure. After his dyspnea worsened last night, diuretics were given and he stabilized somewhat, but fluid management remained tricky. Yu Xiaowen noted this silently and felt intrigued.

events.name: Took the initiative to take over complex patients during ward rounds
events.description: After the shift handover, all the doctors made rounds and arrived at the patient's bedside. When Teacher Li Wei asked who would be willing to take charge of this patient's management, Yu Xiaowen took a deep breath, stepped forward, and said, 'Teacher, I want to try.' She briefly outlined her initial thoughts on volume control, blood glucose monitoring, and nutritional support. Teacher Li Wei nodded approvingly, granted her request, and promised to provide guidance at any time.

events.name: In-depth review of medical records and drawing of the illness chart.
events.description: After returning from the ward, Yu Xiaowen spent the morning sitting at the computer carefully reviewing the patient's complete medical records from the past year, including 3 hospitalization records and monthly outpatient follow-up sheets. On her notebook, she drew a timeline of the patient's progression from elevated creatinine to worsening heart failure, marked key nodes with colored pens, and listed literature questions to investigate.

events.name: Afternoon literature search and data collection
events.description: In the afternoon, she went to the hospital library and searched the literature from the past three years on CNKI and PubMed using 'cardiorenal syndrome' and 'fluid overload' as keywords. She finally selected 5 high-quality reviews and clinical studies, printed and bound them separately, and saved the PDF versions to her USB drive.

events.name: Writing the preliminary analysis framework at night
events.description: After dinner, Yu Xiaowen spread out thick photocopies of medical records and literature in her study and began writing the framework for a case analysis. From disease history features, diagnostic basis, stratified treatment, to prognosis assessment, she wrote nearly a thousand characters. Where she was uncertain, she wrote questions on sticky notes to ask Teacher Li Wei the next day. It was not until 11 p.m. that she rubbed her eyes and closed her computer. During that time, she found the desk lamp was not working and had to dig out a spare LED light as an emergency.

events.name: Ward round report and mentor guidance
events.description: During the morning meeting, Yu Xiaowen reported to her mentor Li Wei her analysis of yesterday's complex case and asked about specific indicators for fluid management. During ward rounds, she paid special attention to the patient's jugular vein, lower limb edema, and urine output records, and suggested a slight increase in the diuretic dose. Li Wei agreed to try it and asked her to record the 24-hour intake and output.

events.name: Light lunch and exchange with colleagues at noon
events.description: At noon, Yu Xiaowen and Wang Fang ate together in the cafeteria. Wang Fang mentioned that the bridesmaid dress color might be champagne. Xiaowen smiled and said, "I've never worn that color before." The two happily discussed amusing things that might happen at the wedding.

events.name: Departmental discussion of difficult cases
events.description: At 3 p.m., during the weekly Tuesday routine difficult-case discussion, Yu Xiaowen mustered the courage to submit this complex case as the main case for discussion. Using a PPT, she quickly presented a chart of the disease progression she had organized and raised three core questions. Department director Zhang Lei and several senior doctors affirmed her work, but also pointed out the anemia factor and calcium-phosphorus metabolism issues she had overlooked, from which Yu Xiaowen benefited greatly.

events.name: Evening walk in the park and listening to music
events.description: Feeling a bit of a headache after work, Yu Xiaowen didn't go straight home but walked into the Culture Park near the hospital. She put on her earphones and played Bach's Cello Suites, then walked briskly along the path for over twenty minutes. The cold air made her thinking much clearer, and her mood settled down.

events.name: Evening supplementary search for absorbing new knowledge
events.description: After returning home and having a simple dinner, Yu Xiaowen immediately turned on her computer. Based on the keywords anemia and CKD-MBD (chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder) mentioned in the afternoon discussion, she searched several references again. She added new paragraphs about the use of erythropoietin and phosphate binders to the original analysis framework, and adjusted the treatment priority order.

After exercising, they bought fruit together and went home to make a healthy salad, balancing work and rest.

events.name: Morning ward rounds and treatment adjustments
events.description: After the morning meeting, Yu Xiaowen went straight to the ward to check the effect of yesterday’s diuretic adjustment. The patient’s urine output from last night to this morning was about 1500 ml, the edema in both lower limbs had markedly subsided, and shortness of breath had eased. She reported this to Li Wei and suggested maintaining today’s dosage and adding electrolyte tests. Her supervisor agreed. In the morning, she also handled daily issues for several regular patients.

events.name: Invite the nutrition department for consultation
events.description: Considering the patient's renal failure and diabetes, at 10 a.m. Yu Xiaowen sent a nutrition department consultation request through the hospital information system, stating that assistance was needed in developing a low-protein, low-sodium, high-quality-protein diabetic diet plan, and included her mobile number for contact.

events.name: Went to the badminton hall after work.
events.description: Got off work at 5:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowen drove home and changed into her sports gear, then walked to the badminton hall at the nearby Zhongyuan District Experimental Primary School. Lin Wei had already arrived early and was warming up at the side of the court. After high-fiving, the two started warming up with high clears.

events.name: Exhilarating doubles practice
events.description: The gym was not crowded that night, and they joined a mixed doubles group. Yu Xiaowen mainly covered the front court, while Lin Wei smashed from the back court; they were well-coordinated. The two sides went back and forth and played three full games, lasting an hour and a half. Sweat soaked their sportswear, but it felt extremely exhilarating. At the end, Lin Wei praised Xiaowen for much quicker reactions at the net and introduced a new badminton partner—Xiao Zhou, a nurse from the surgery department—so they could play together in the future.

events.name: Buy fresh fruit
events.description: After playing, the two went to the fruit shop at the entrance of the badminton hall. Yu Xiaowen picked apples, bananas, and blueberries, while Lin Wei bought a box of strawberries. Laughing, they discussed which fruit would make a better smoothie, then each took their bags and said goodbye.

events.name: Homemade fruit salad as a late-night snack.
events.description: Back at the apartment, Yu Xiaowen first washed and cut up the fruit: sliced the banana, cored and diced the apple, added a handful of blueberries, and mixed in low-fat yogurt. She sat on the sofa, eating the salad while reading the chat history of the badminton group "Badminton Trio" on her phone. Xu Tao had posted a short video of himself playing in Shenzhen, and she casually gave it a like.

2025-01.daily_overview: After the morning ward rounds, I attended a lecture on hypertension prevention and treatment given by Dr. Liu Qiang in the afternoon and gained a lot; in the evening, I attended the third pottery class, learned coil building, and made a small vase blank.

events.name: Morning routine medical work and credit card repayment
events.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowen attended the morning meeting on time. During the subsequent ward round, she reassessed the electrolyte results of a complicated case, found that the blood potassium was slightly high, so she suspended the diuretic and added a potassium-lowering resin. After that, she quickly handled a few simple outpatient follow-up patients and wrote a transfer note. During her free time in the morning, she paid last month's credit card bill through mobile banking, confirming that the spending was mainly on supermarkets and book purchases.

events.name: Dr. Liu Qiang's hypertension lecture
events.description: At 3:00 p.m., the department's professional study session was held in the meeting room on the 15th floor. Dr. Liu Qiang had prepared a beautiful PPT and gave an in-depth explanation of the 2024 edition of the Chinese Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of Hypertension, focusing on the evidence basis and clinical translation of combined ACEI and CCB therapy. Yu Xiaowen sat in the front row and filled three full pages of notes, especially highlighting the management flowchart for elderly hypertensive patients.

events.name: Ask questions privately after the lecture.
events.description: As soon as the lecture ended, Yu Xiaowen quickly walked to the podium and asked Dr. Liu Qiang two specific questions: 'For elderly patients with diabetic nephropathy, how should the initial combination therapy dosage be determined?' and 'When ACEI causes an intolerable dry cough, can it be switched to ARB or ARNI started directly?' Dr. Liu patiently answered and recommended two related RCT papers. Xiaowen carefully noted down the index numbers.

events.name: Digitized the evening lecture notes
events.description: After getting home from work, Yu Xiaowen had a simple dinner, then opened her computer and notebook and organized the afternoon lecture content into a mind map, adding literature links to key knowledge points. When finished, she sent it to the department's study group and got a like from Wang Fang.

events.name: Third pottery class: coil-built bottle.
events.description: At 7 PM pottery class, Teacher Zheng taught everyone the coil-building method: first roll the clay into long strips of even thickness, then coil them up layer by layer, using slip to bond them. Yu Xiaowen planned to make a small vase 20 cm tall. She rolled nearly twenty coils and carefully built them up, nearly collapsing several times, but with the teacher's help she reinforced the base. The final vase's rough shape was crooked but rather artistic, and Su Ya joked beside her, calling it 'post-modernism'.

In the evening, browsed the internet alone for bridesmaid gift inspiration. Both career and friendship were fruitful, but after sitting for a long time, neck and shoulder soreness set in.

events.name: Submitted the report and received high praise.
events.description: After the morning meeting, Yu Xiaowen printed the revised and improved case analysis report into a booklet and handed it to Teacher Li Wei with both hands. Teacher Li flipped through it carefully for ten minutes, nodding from time to time. Finally, she closed the report and said with a smile, "The differential diagnosis is very thorough, and the literature you consulted is up to date. It looks like you've put in the effort. If you turn this into a case report, it will be no problem to submit." Xiaowen was pleasantly surprised and said she was willing to try.

events.name: Attended this week's departmental quality control meeting.
events.description: At 10 a.m., the department held its monthly quality control meeting to analyze last month's medical record writing issues. Yu Xiaowen was singled out for praise; the three discharge records she wrote were rated Grade A, and Director Zhang Lei encouraged the younger doctors to learn from her. She lowered her head a little sheepishly.

events.name: Finalize bridesmaid arrangements at lunch
events.description: At noon, Yu Xiaowen and Wang Fang sat facing each other in the cafeteria. Wang Fang handed over a folder containing sample photos from several wedding companies. While eating, they discussed bridesmaid dress styles—Wang Fang preferred a champagne-colored satin long dress, while Yu Xiaowen suggested pairing it with pearl earrings. They decided to wait until spring warmed up before going to the stores to try them on, and for now they saved their favorite styles on their phones. Xiaowen readily agreed and also volunteered to make the digital photo album to be played at the wedding.

events.name: In the afternoon, organize case image materials and the hypoglycemia episode.
events.description: In the afternoon, Yu Xiaowen retrieved all the imaging data for the complex case from the medical records office, including electronic images of the chest X-ray and echocardiogram. After two hours of continuous work, she felt slightly dizzy and realized that her lunch had been digested too quickly, and it might be hypoglycemia. She quickly took out a spare chocolate from the drawer and ate it, and felt better after resting for a few minutes.

events.name: Evening search for bridesmaid inspiration and neck and shoulder soreness flare-up
events.description: After getting home from work, Yu Xiaowen curled up on the sofa and opened Xiaohongshu and Taobao, searching keywords such as 'bridesmaid dress champagne color' and 'handmade bridesmaid gifts'. She browsed for nearly two hours straight. When she put down her phone, she felt obvious soreness in her neck and shoulders. When she tried to turn her neck, she heard a cracking noise. She quickly did several sets of relaxation exercises and applied a hot towel for 15 minutes, which only slightly relieved the discomfort. She wrote in her diary: long periods of desk work require vigilance.

2025-01.daily_overview: After the morning run, she attended the last introductory pottery class and successfully made a cup on the pottery wheel. After class, she went shopping and had a meal with her best friend Zhang Jing, enjoying a weekend of girl time, and called her parents far away to share the joy.

events.name: Persisted in the morning run and neck and shoulder stretches in the cold wind.
events.description: At 7 a.m., Yu Xiaowen wrapped her exercise jacket tightly and went out for a jog along Jingsan Road. The cold wind cut her face like a knife, but she persisted until she turned back at Dongfengqu Park, covering about 3 kilometers in total. After returning home, she did 10 minutes of neck and shoulder stretches; the soreness from yesterday had mostly eased.

events.name: Last introductory class: throwing a cup on the wheel
events.description: At 9 a.m., the fourth class began. Teacher Zheng Guodong taught everyone to make cups using an electric potter's wheel. Under the teacher's hands-on guidance, Yu Xiaowen carefully controlled the speed with the foot pedal, holding the clay steadily with both hands, from opening to pulling up, the clay slowly rose in her hands and took the shape of a cup. Although the cup wall tilted slightly midway and she corrected it in time, in the end a cup with smooth lines was finished, and she was so excited she almost cheered. Su Ya also successfully pulled a goblet nearby. After class, the two took a photo with the teacher and agreed to continue in the advanced class.

events.name: Clean up and say goodbye to the studio.
events.description: After class, Yu Xiaowen carefully cleaned her workbench and the pottery wheel, and placed the four semi-finished pieces she had made earlier—a small bowl, a tea cup, a vase, and a ceramic mug—on the shelf to await firing. She thanked Teacher Zheng, who encouraged her to come to the studio's open day to practice whenever she had time. She promised to come pick up her pieces when they were fired at the end of the month.

events.name: Shopping with her best friend Zhang Jing
events.description: At noon, Yu Xiaowen drove to David City to meet Zhang Jing. They first tried lipstick in the cosmetics section on the first floor, then helped each other choose and try on new down jackets in the women's clothing section on the second floor. Zhang Jing picked a long white one, while Xiaowen took a liking to a short beige one. As they shopped and chatted, Xiaowen poured out stories about her pottery class and Wang Fang being a bridesmaid. Zhang Jing listened with great interest and even volunteered to help advise on the bridesmaid gift.

events.name: Enjoying sweet and sour pork at a restaurant
events.description: At 3 p.m., the two sat down at a Chinese restaurant on the fourth floor of David City. Yu Xiaowen ordered sweet and sour pork tenderloin without hesitation, and Zhang Jing added a bowl of hot and sour soup and greens. When the dishes arrived, the tenderloin was crispy on the outside and tender inside, with a pleasant sweet-and-sour taste. Xiaowen ate heartily, saying it was the most satisfying meal of the week. During the meal, they discussed their plans for the Spring Festival and agreed to visit the New Year goods market at Guomao 360 before the holiday.

events.name: Call parents upon arriving home
events.description: At 5 p.m., Yu Xiaowen returned home. She first hung up the newly bought down jacket, then sat on the sofa and called her father, Yu Jianguo. In the video, her father was practicing calligraphy and looked in good spirits. She excitedly showed him photos of the ceramic cup she had made today. Her father praised her skillful hands and told her not to work too hard. She also chatted with her mother for a few minutes, who reminded her to dress warmly when the temperature dropped next week. After hanging up, she felt warm inside.

2025-01.daily_overview: After sleeping in on the weekend, she received a book sent by a close friend from afar. In the afternoon, she communicated with her financial advisor about adjusting investments. In the evening, she sorted through her pottery pieces, shared them with family and friends, and read the new book until late at night.

events.name: Receive a gift from a distant place.
events.description: At 10 a.m., the courier knocked and delivered a cardboard box. Yu Xiaowen opened it and found it was sent by Wang Lina: a copy of Atul Gawande's Better and a handwritten card that read, "Dear Wen, last year you said you wanted to improve your professional competence. This book should suit you. Miss you, see you at the New Year!" She immediately took a photo and sent it on WeChat to thank her, and the two then had half an hour of voice chat, during which Lina also asked about her father Yu Jianguo's blood sugar.

events.name: Household cleaning and breakfast
events.description: After hanging up, Yu Xiaowen toasted two slices of whole wheat bread for herself, fried an egg, and made a cup of coffee. After eating, she vacuumed the whole apartment with a cordless vacuum cleaner, wiped the bookshelf and windowsills with a damp cloth, and opened the windows to air the place. The winter sunlight streamed in, leaving the whole room bright and tidy.

events.name: Monthly wealth management communication.
events.description: At 2 p.m., as agreed, she communicated with Wang Mingyuan, a wealth management advisor at China Merchants Bank, via WeChat. Mingyuan sent this month's market briefing and noted recent volatility in the bond market. Yu Xiaowen checked the performance of the two bond funds she held, and one of them had declined noticeably in returns. Following Mingyuan's advice, she decided to reduce the monthly investment ratio for that fund from 30% to 15% and allocate the freed-up funds to a more stable money market fund. She completed the operation through mobile banking and set the 15th of each month as her fund adjustment day.

events.name: Brother video-called to share recent news
events.description: At 4 p.m., she received a video call from her brother Yu Xiaofeng. He had just finished overtime work in Shenzhen, looking tired. He showed her the interface of a smart home app he had newly developed. Yu Xiaowen, showing great interest, offered several user experience suggestions. Her brother asked about their parents' health, and after she told him they were fine, they agreed to definitely return to Luoyang for a reunion during the Spring Festival.

events.name: Organizing pottery works collection and clearing out expired food
events.description: At 4:30, Yu Xiaowen imported the photos of works taken during the four classes from her phone into her computer, used photo-editing software to crop and adjust colors, and created a simple electronic photo album. Then she checked the kitchen, found a box of yogurt and a bag of lettuce that had expired, cleaned them up and threw them into the trash, reminding herself to buy things only as needed in the future.

events.name: Evening immersive reading
events.description: After dinner, Yu Xiaowen took a shower, put on her pajamas, leaned against the headboard, and opened "Better: A Surgeon's Notes on Performance". The opening describes how a surgeon improved his surgical skills by collecting feedback data. She thought of the cases she had organized, began marking interesting parts with a highlighter, and wrote reflections in the margins. Before she knew it, she read until 11 p.m., and only closed the book and fell asleep when her eyelids were heavy.

2025-01.daily_overview: Yu Xiaowen spent the whole day integrating her previous research and work from the past few days, wrote the first draft of a clinical report on a complex case, and did the final polishing at home in the evening.

events.name: Morning ward rounds and case follow-up
events.description: After the shift handover, Yu Xiaowen first went to check on a patient with a complex case and found that the patient's weight had increased by 0.5 kg, possibly mild fluid retention. She decided to resume a low-dose diuretic. She recorded the observation in the progress notes and attached the latest lab reports to the report draft.

events.name: Writing the first draft of the report (devoting the entire lunch break)
events.description: Starting at 10 a.m., Yu Xiaowen turned off the music on her phone and focused on writing the case report. She integrated the earlier analytical framework, discussion meeting opinions, literature evidence, and laboratory data into a complete draft. During the lunch break, she didn't go to the cafeteria but asked Wang Fang to bring her two buns, eating while writing in the office. When Wang Fang brought the buns, she also gave her a box of yogurt and told her to take care of herself. By 4 p.m., a nearly 3,000-word draft report (including abstract, medical history, diagnosis and treatment process, differential diagnosis, and discussion) had basically taken shape.

events.name: A brief evening walk to clear the mind.
events.description: At 4:30 p.m., her eyes felt sore and strained, so she walked two laps around the hospital garden. Some wintersweet had bloomed, releasing a refreshing fragrance. She took a few deep breaths of fresh air, emptied her mind, and prepared for the final examination.

events.name: In the evening, finalize the document and send it to the supervisor.
events.description: When she got home in the evening, Yu Xiaowen printed out the report, went through it herself with a red pen, and corrected a few typos and logical transitions. She then sent the electronic version to Dr. Li Wei's hospital email with the message, 'Teacher, the first draft of the complex case report is complete. I sincerely request your review and guidance.' After sending it, she let out a long breath, feeling a weight lifted off her shoulders. Before bed, she deliberately did 5 minutes of neck and shoulder stretches to avoid a recurrence of her old injury.

2025-01.daily_overview: Submitted the report to Teacher Li Wei for detailed guidance and was inspired by his suggestions on submitting the paper; in the afternoon, revised and polished it and did preliminary research on target journals; in the evening, continued reading "Better: A Surgeon's Notes on Performance."

events.name: Submitted the report at the morning meeting and received approval comments.
events.description: In the morning, Teacher Li Wei sent someone to return the printed report, which was covered in red annotations. Yu Xiaowen opened it with reverence and saw that Teacher Li had written in the differential diagnosis section: 'The logic is clear here, but the analysis of the novel heart failure marker ST2 is missing; this can be added.' In the discussion section, he wrote: 'It is recommended to incorporate the latest 2024 KDIGO guideline perspectives and to consider how to turn this case into a publishable case report.' The final overall comment was: 'An excellent demonstration of clinical thinking. After revision, you may try submitting it to provincial journals such as Henan Medical Research.'

events.name: Morning ward rounds and seeing new patients
events.description: After reading the annotations, Yu Xiaowen first handled her daily work. During ward rounds, the patient's cardiac function was stabilizing, which slightly relieved her. She then saw a newly admitted patient with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and wrote admission orders. In the midst of her busy work, she accidentally knocked over her water cup, but luckily she wiped it up in time and the documents were unharmed.

events.name: Focused on revising the report
events.description: In the afternoon, she revised the manuscript point by point according to the comments, added the ST2 analysis section, and looked up the latest KDIGO guidelines online to update the discussion section. It took more than two hours to complete the revised draft, which she named 'Final Version - Pending Submission', and marked the data that needed further verification (such as the impact of patients' economic status on adherence). She planned to consult the Medical Affairs Department the next day. During this time, she felt her eyes become dry, so she applied eye drops and rested briefly.

events.name: Initial screening for journal submission and a call with Sun Yue
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowen searches the hospital intranet for the hospital's incentive policies for published papers, then logs in to Wanfang and VIP to check the submission requirements for Henan Medical Research and the Chinese Journal of Internal Medicine. She compares the review cycles and page charges and decides to submit to the former first. After work, she receives a call from Sun Yue. They chat for a while, and Sun Yue says she wants to visit her this weekend. She gladly agrees, and they make plans to cook together on Saturday.

events.name: Continued reading and note-taking in the evening.
events.description: After returning home, she continued reading Chapters 2 and 3 of Better: A Surgeon's Notes on Performance. The content about medical team communication and continuous learning resonated deeply with her. She copied several aphorisms into her notebook and wrote down her reflection for the day: 'Learn to grow from criticism, just as from medical cases.' Because she was so absorbed in thinking, she went to bed half an hour later than usual.

2025-01.daily_overview: After a morning run, worked normally and planned follow-up treatment for cases; at noon, suddenly received the news of her father's cerebral infarction, urgently took leave and returned to Luoyang by high-speed rail, went straight to the hospital, and accompanied him day and night, anxious yet strong.

events.name: Morning jog along the riverbank
events.description: At 6:40 in the morning, Yu Xiaowen put on her sportswear as usual and jogged along the banks of the Jinshui River. Today she quickened her pace, covering 5 kilometers in about 30 minutes with a steady heart rate. After the run, she did a set of stretches, paying special attention to relaxing her neck and shoulders, and felt light and agile.

events.name: Morning routine clinical work
events.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowen attended the morning meeting as usual. During rounds, she paid close attention to the complex case patient and found that the patient reported improved appetite and reduced edema in the right lower limb. Lab results showed plasma BNP dropped from 1800 pg/mL to 800 pg/mL, so she planned to add an oral medication in the afternoon. Afterwards, she handled two consultation records and reviewed the paper she intended to submit, planning to submit it the next day.

events.name: Received an urgent call from her mother
events.description: At 12:15 p.m., Yu Xiaowen had just finished her homemade lunch in the duty room of the inpatient department when her phone rang urgently. The screen showed "Mom." When she answered, she heard her mother's trembling voice on the other end: "Wenwen, your dad suddenly can't move and can't speak clearly. He's just been sent to Luoyang Central Hospital, and they say it's a stroke..." It hit her like a heavy blow, and her heart sank. But her professional instinct made her quickly ask for the key information: "What time did it start? Has thrombolysis been done?" When she learned that thrombolysis had been started within one hour of onset, she breathed a slight sigh of relief, but still decisively decided to go back immediately.

events.name: Emergency leave request and work handover.
events.description: After hanging up the phone, she hurried to the director's office, where Director Zhang Lei was reviewing documents. With red-rimmed eyes, she quickly explained the situation. Director Zhang approved her leave on the spot and told her to go without worry; her colleagues would cover matters at the hospital. She returned to her office, entered the important tasks at hand into the handover notebook one by one, handed the key points of the nursing plans for complex cases to Wang Fang, and showed Liu Qiang where the desktop folders were. Within minutes the handover was done, and she quickly took off her white coat, grabbed her backpack, and rushed out of the ward.

events.name: Racing against the clock to get to Luoyang
events.description: At the hospital entrance, she first used her phone to buy a ticket on the next high-speed train, the 13:05 from Zhengzhou East to Luoyang Longmen, then hailed a taxi and rushed to the east station. In the taxi, she sent a voice message to her mother with trembling hands: 'Mom, I'm taking the 1 p.m. high-speed train, and I'll be there shortly before 2. Is Dad conscious now? You must stay calm.' On the way, she used her phone to search for information such as 'precautions after cerebral infarction thrombolysis' and 'secondary prevention of cerebral infarction,' and saved screenshots of key points. The high-speed train arrived at 13:45, and she rushed out of the station and took a taxi straight to Luoyang Central Hospital.

events.name: Meeting in the ward and understanding the condition
events.description: At 2:30 in the afternoon, Yu Xiaowen ran breathlessly to the neurology ward. Her mother, Li Xiuying, rushed over and poured out her grief as soon as she saw her. Xiaowen hugged her mother tightly for a few seconds, then urged her to sit down. She walked to the bedside and saw her father, Yu Jianguo, lying with his eyes closed, his left limbs limp and the corner of his mouth slightly crooked. She leaned down and softly called, Dad, I'm back. Her father opened his eyes slightly and let out a vague ah, with tears seeping from the corners of his eyes. The attending physician then explained the condition in detail: diffusion-weighted imaging suggested a right thalamic lacunar infarction, post-thrombolysis vessel recanalization was assessed as good, and the hemiplegia and aphasia still needed observation for recovery. Yu Xiaowen followed up with professional terms about blood pressure control and blood lipid status, and the doctor answered each question one by one.

events.name: Discussing treatment and rehabilitation plans
events.description: In the evening, in the corridor outside the ward, Yu Xiaowen discussed with her mother and decided not to transfer hospitals for now, but first stabilize treatment at Luoyang Central Hospital and consider Zhengzhou later depending on the recovery situation. She borrowed a computer in the doctors' office to look up the contact information of the hospital's Department of Neurology, planning to call the next day for a consultation. At the same time, she created a family WeChat group called Let Dad Stand Up, added her brother Yu Xiaofeng and her sister-in-law to the group, uploaded her father's latest physical examination report, and explained the initial treatment plan. Her brother immediately replied: I will ask for leave right away and arrive the day after tomorrow at the earliest. Xiaowen replied: No rush, take care of your work first, I will handle things here, but deep down she longed for her brother to come.

events.name: Nighttime care and mood journaling.
events.description: Late at night, Xiaowen persuaded her mother to go home and rest, and she stayed alone in the ward to keep watch. She pulled over a companion chair and sat beside her father’s bed, turned on the small lamp her parents had brought, and opened Better, but couldn’t read a single word. Then she took out her diary and wrote, ‘2025.1.15, the longest day of my life. Dad collapsed. I know my role has to become bigger from this moment on. I cannot fall.’ Closing the notebook, she held her father’s hand and listened to the rhythmic sound of the monitor.

During breaks in caring for him, she began reading “Better,” drawing professional strength from the words. Meanwhile, her lower back began to ache faintly from sitting too long, so she moved around a little.

events.name: Accompanying patients in the ward and reading Better: A Surgeon's Notes on Performance
events.description: On January 16, 2025, Yu Xiaowen was accompanying her father Yu Jianguo, whose condition was gradually stabilizing, in the ward of Luoyang Central Hospital. During a break in caregiving, she took out Better, which her friend Wang Lina had sent earlier, and began reading it carefully, noting her initial thoughts. She noticed the book's viewpoints on physicians' self-improvement, thought of how she had responded to her father's sudden cerebral infarction, and silently resolved to study cardiovascular and cerebrovascular emergency management more systematically.

events.name: Discussed father's condition with mother.
events.description: At noon, her mother, Li Xiuying, brought millet porridge she had personally made. While her father was eating, Yu Xiaowen quietly talked with her mother in the corridor about the doctor's morning ward-round opinions, and learned that the thrombolysis had worked well but that he still needed to be closely observed for 48 hours. She comforted her mother, saying not to worry too much and that she would stay in the ward the whole time.

events.name: Do some simple waist stretches in the corridor
events.description: After sitting for a long time in the afternoon, Yu Xiaowen got up to fetch water and felt some stiffness in her lower back. She then did a few simple side bends and rotations in the corridor outside the ward, and the soreness eased a little. She thought to herself that once her father got better, she must resume regular stretching.

events.name: Read deeply into “Better: A Surgeon’s Notes on Performance” and made annotations
events.description: On January 17, 2025, Yu Xiaowen continued to accompany her father in the ward and used the intervals when the nurse changed dressings and her father took a nap to read Better in depth. events.name: Preparing to listen to classical music to ease emotions.
events.description: Late at night on January 17, 2025, Yu Xiaowen was accompanying her father, Yu Jianguo, in his ward at Luoyang Central Hospital. Days of worry and exhaustion left her anxious and restless. She decided to ease her emotions by listening to classical music, so she took her earphones out of her bag, connected them to her phone, opened the music player, found Debussy's 'Clair de Lune', and prepared to play it.

events.name: Listening to Debussy's ‘Clair de Lune’ for solace
events.description: Yu Xiaowen put on her headphones, gently pressed play, and the melody of Debussy's "Moonlight" flowed out slowly. She closed her eyes, leaned back in the chair by the hospital bed, and let the music soothe her inner anxiety and fatigue. In the quiet ward, she felt a long-missed sense of peace and comfort for the first time, and the music accompanied her through the late-night hours. She decided to listen to a piece of classical music every night before bed to help her sleep.
