2025-12.daily_overview: A compensatory rest day: after an early morning run along the river, I enjoyed music and tea on the balcony with deep reading; in the afternoon, I summarized the results of my dietary adjustments; in the evening, I had a video call with my parents about my father's rehabilitation costs. A quiet and introspective day.

events.name: Morning run and post-run cooldown
events.description: Got up at 6:40 a.m., drank a glass of warm water, then went out for a 3-kilometer jog along the Jinshui River, keeping her heart rate at around 140 bpm. After running, she stretched carefully and went home for a shower.

events.name: Balcony music tea break and deep reading
events.description: At 9 a.m., Yu Xiaowen laid out a soft mat on her apartment balcony, took out Jin Jun Mei tea and a kung fu tea set from the tea cabinet, boiled water, and brewed a pot of bright orange-yellow tea. She connected her phone to the Bluetooth speaker and played Bach's Cello Suites. Amid the deep, flowing cello music, she opened The Birth of the Clinic, which had been left unread for a long time, and read while making pencil annotations in the margins, deeply experiencing Foucault's deconstruction of medical history. After about an hour, she switched to a light book, An Introduction to Pottery and Beyond, browsing images of hand-building techniques and glaze color combinations, imagining new shapes she might try at her next pottery class.

events.name: Writing a mood diary
events.description: After finishing the book, Yu Xiaowen stayed at the balcony desk, took out her lake-blue cloth-covered diary, and wrote down today's thoughts: "The moment when tea fragrance, book pages, and string music resonate together is a gift from life." She briefly reviewed her reading reflections and her longing for pottery, expressing her appreciation for this peaceful time.

events.name: Interim self-summary of dietary adjustments
events.description: In the afternoon, Yu Xiaowen reviewed her diet diary and physical sensations recorded over the past month or more in her study, including her iron supplement intake and consumption of iron-rich foods such as red meat and pork liver. She felt her energy had improved significantly, dizziness and fatigue had disappeared, and her complexion had become ruddier. She wrote a summary in her diary and decided to continue her good eating habits to provide a physical foundation for preparing for the attending physician examination.

events.name: Video call with parents to discuss rehabilitation expenses and family plans.
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowen proactively made a WeChat video call to her mother Li Xiuying and had a three-way call with her parents at their home in Luoyang. She asked in detail about her father Yu Jianguo's recent rehabilitation progress, the estimated costs of subsequent physical therapy and re-examinations, and the ongoing expenses of daily care. Her mother answered each question, and her father added that his legs felt stronger. Yu Xiaowen recorded all of this in her phone memo so that she could provide the information the next day when discussing with her financial advisor. The call lasted about 40 minutes; at the end, her mother reminded her to rest well over the weekend.

2025-12.daily_overview: After catching up on sleep following a night shift, she did a simple Baduanjin stretching routine in the morning. In the afternoon, she brought her financial documents to meet a financial advisor and adjusted priorities. In the evening, she handled detailed financial decisions and received a notice about the department dinner, establishing her parents' medical reserve fund as the top priority of the year.

events.name: Rest at home after the night shift and practice Baduanjin.
events.description: After finishing her night shift in the early morning, Yu Xiaowen drove home to Jinshui District, exhausted. After a quick wash, she went straight to bed and slept until 11 a.m. When she woke up, her body felt stiff, so she did 10 minutes of Baduanjin in the living room and used a foam roller to relax her back. Then she boiled a bowl of frozen dumplings for brunch and made a cup of Jin Junmei tea to refresh herself.

events.name: Received the sales list from the pottery exhibition and confirmed receipt of payment.
events.description: At noon, Yu Xiaowen received a WeChat message from Teacher Zheng Guodong with the sales details of the pottery exhibition: 4 custom-patterned zodiac rooster ceramic plates sold for a total of 3,200 yuan; after deducting the studio's 20% material and firing fee, the net amount was 2,560 yuan; colleague Wang Fang bought a small cup for 150 yuan; the total to be credited was 2,710 yuan. Yu Xiaowen checked and found it correct, then replied to confirm.

events.name: Go to the bank to meet with financial advisor Wang Mingyuan.
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowen drove as scheduled to the Private Banking Department of China Merchants Bank in Zhengdong New District for her annual meeting with financial advisor Wang Mingyuan. She clearly stated that the parents' medical reserve fund should be the top priority, and moved the previously envisioned home down payment plan to a later date. Based on the current total savings of about 120,000 yuan, annual income, and expenses, the two initially discussed a conservative allocation plan that would increase monthly dedicated savings and maintain the fund's regular investment plan but at a reduced proportion. Wang Mingyuan noted the key points of the plan and agreed to organize them into a document and send it. The meeting lasted about an hour.

events.name: Read the financial summary and decide priorities
events.description: Back home, Yu Xiaowen sat on the sofa and carefully read the year-end financial summary sent by Wang Mingyuan on her phone, including the annual income and expense analysis, fund returns, and suggestions. After repeatedly considering her father's potential rehabilitation and nursing needs in the future, she called Wang Mingyuan to further consult about fund returns and the size of the medical reserve fund. Wang Mingyuan explained the current market from a professional perspective and estimated the required amount. Yu Xiaowen expressed her concerns about her parents' health and made it clear that family security comes first.

events.name: Create a written financial plan for the new year and reply to the advisor
events.description: After hanging up, Yu Xiaowen took out her financial planning notebook in the study and wrote down “2026 Financial Priorities: 1. Parents' medical reserve fund (mandatory savings of at least 2,500 yuan per month); 2. Keep the existing fund automatic investment plan but stop adding more; pause active saving for a home down payment; 3. Maintain an emergency fund with ample liquidity.” Then she replied to Wang Mingyuan via WeChat, informing him of her decision and thanking him for his professional advice, and they agreed to refine the installment plan after the New Year.

events.name: Received notice of the department's year-end gathering.
events.description: In the evening, department director Zhang Lei posted a notice in the hospital's internal work group: the department year-end dinner would be held at a restaurant in Zhongyuan Wanda Plaza at 7 p.m. on December 27, with the agenda including annual summary, lucky draw, and free discussion. Yu Xiaowen replied "Confirm attendance" in the group and decided to relax well with her colleagues at that time.

2025-12.daily_overview: On the Winter Solstice, after morning Baduanjin, she organized the activity report materials for the nursing home in the morning, received the pottery exhibition income and transferred it to a dedicated savings account, and adjusted the monthly budget; in the evening, she made dumplings alone to celebrate the festival and shared with her parents via video call. The traditional ritual was filled with warmth.

events.name: Morning Baduanjin and meditation
events.description: Got up at 7:30, practiced a set of Baduanjin first, then did ten minutes of mindfulness meditation to bring calm to the day.

events.name: Prepared the report document for the nursing home pottery activity.
events.description: In the morning, Yu Xiaowen worked overtime in the resident doctors' on-duty room at Zhengzhou Central Hospital, compiling positive feedback from the pottery activity previously held at the nursing home, including specific examples of improved participation and emotional well-being among the elderly, as well as photo comparisons. She created a concise PPT draft to prepare for the in-depth discussion with the rehabilitation department director the next day, which took nearly three hours.

events.name: Confirmed the income from the pottery exhibition and transferred it to the dedicated account.
events.description: During a break at work, Yu Xiaowen checked her mobile banking app and confirmed that the 2,710 yuan transferred by Teacher Zheng Guodong had arrived. She took a screenshot to save the receipt, then replied to Teacher Zheng and Wang Fang on WeChat to confirm receipt. After returning home from work, she transferred the entire amount into a separate savings account under her own name (for a special dream fund), and wrote in her notes app: “Income from pottery exhibition sales, intended for next year's advanced pottery course.”

events.name: Adjusted the monthly budget according to the new plan.
events.description: In the home study in the afternoon, Yu Xiaowen reviewed the plan drawn up with Wang Mingyuan and reorganized the monthly income and expenses: after listing fixed expenditures such as rent, living expenses, and car maintenance, she decided to prioritize transferring 2,500 yuan each month to a dedicated medical reserve account for her parents, maintain a 2,000 yuan monthly fund investment plan, change the previous house down payment savings to a minimum monthly amount of 1,000 yuan, and cut unnecessary spending. She drew a detailed arrow flowchart in her financial planning notebook.

events.name: On the Winter Solstice, she made dumplings alone and shared with her parents via video
events.description: In the evening, Yu Xiaowen went to a nearby supermarket and bought pork, Chinese cabbage, and flour. After returning home, she put on an apron and kneaded dough, made filling, and wrapped dumplings by herself. Her technique was unpracticed, but she was earnest. At around 7, the dumplings were ready. She filled a plate, then video-called her parents in Luoyang on her phone to show them her work. Her mother, Li Xiuying, smiled and gave instructions on the screen, and her father, Yu Jianguo, praised her for growing up. Through the video call, the family “ate” dumplings together, making up for the regret of not being able to reunite.

events.name: Writing down the financial blueprint
events.description: After dinner, Yu Xiaowen neatly copied the priorities and monthly plan confirmed that day into her finance notebook, then stuck on a pink index label reading 2026 starts today. After closing the notebook, she got ready to wash up and get enough rest for work the next day.

2025-12.daily_overview: A workday in the rehabilitation department. After an early morning run, she had an in-depth discussion with the department director in the morning about the nursing home feedback and received support to launch the art therapy research. In the afternoon, she designed a questionnaire plan based on this and, outside of work, recorded the funding arrangements for pottery training. It was a busy but constructive day.

events.name: Morning run and morning study
events.description: Got up at 6:30, drank a glass of warm water, and went for a 3 km jog along the Jinshui River at a pace of about 7 min/km. After the run, returned home for a quick shower, and during breakfast spent 15 minutes on medical English vocabulary on her phone.

events.name: Discussed feedback from the nursing home with Wang Jianguo, director of the rehabilitation department.
events.description: At 10 a.m., Yu Xiaowen took the compiled feedback materials from the nursing home pottery activity to the director's office, where she reported to Director Wang Jianguo the positive effects of the activity: many elderly residents showed improved finger flexibility and significantly elevated mood. Director Wang highly approved and believed that these first-hand experiences could serve as an empirical basis for advancing the art therapy questionnaire survey. He suggested that she first conduct an in-hospital questionnaire on 'stroke patients' acceptance of pottery intervention during rehabilitation' as preliminary preparation for applying for the Youth Fund. Deeply encouraged, Yu Xiaowen carefully noted down the director's guidance.

events.name: Conceive a questionnaire survey plan for art therapy
events.description: After talking with the director, Yu Xiaowen returned to her desk and began drafting the questionnaire survey plan according to the director's instructions. She listed the survey purpose, target population (stroke patients and their families in the rehabilitation ward), and questionnaire dimensions (cognitive interest, feasibility perception, barrier factors, support needs), planned to use the Likert scale, and estimated the sample size. With most of the initial framework completed, she decided to contact her college classmate Zhou Haoran, who was good at research design, in the evening to improve it together.

events.name: Recording pottery study funds and plans
events.description: While eating lunch in the cafeteria, Yu Xiaowen wrote in both her phone memo and her portable notebook: 2,710 yuan was added to her savings account, earmarked specifically for next year's pottery course training. She checked that the intermediate course at Teacher Zheng Guodong's studio costs about 2,500 yuan, confirmed the funds were sufficient, and set the goal of signing up in the first quarter of next year.

events.name: Routine ward round and progress notes
events.description: In the afternoon she attended the departmental regular meeting, then assisted Dr. Li Wei with rehabilitation assessments for two newly transferred patients. She recorded the assessment results and short-term rehabilitation goals in detail in the electronic medical records. Before getting off work, Wang Fang stopped by and invited her to dinner on Friday evening, and she smiled and agreed.

events.name: Daily communication with patients in the rehabilitation department.
events.description: During the morning ward rounds, Yu Xiaowen paid special attention to an elderly stroke patient who was resistant to rehabilitation training. She tried to encourage the elderly patient using her previous pottery activity example from the nursing home, and the patient expressed willingness to try fine hand movements. She recorded this observation in her work log.

events.name: Video-called my mother to discuss family matters.
events.description: At 8 p.m., Yu Xiaowen made a WeChat video call to her mother from her study. Her mother, Li Xiuying, answered at home in Xigong District, Luoyang, and showed on camera the Laba garlic she had pickled and the dumplings she had just wrapped. The mother and daughter agreed: Yu Xiaowen would return to Luoyang on the 30th at the end of the month and stay two days to spend New Year's Day with her parents; her father's next follow-up appointment was set for January 5, and Yu Xiaowen needed to accompany him; the Spring Festival dinner menu was initially sketched out, including hulatang, braised noodles, sweet and sour pork, and other dishes her daughter liked. Yu Xiaowen wrote down the key points one by one. Finally, her mother reminded her not to work too hard, and they said goodbye with smiles.

events.name: Contact classmate Zhou Haoran to collaborate on designing the questionnaire
events.description: At 9:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowen contacted her university classmate Zhou Haoran, who works at the National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases in Beijing, via WeChat video call, explained her idea for an art therapy questionnaire survey, and invited him to help design it. With his extensive research experience, Zhou Haoran suggested using a Likert 5-point scale and helped her determine the four dimensions of the questionnaire (interest awareness, feasibility, barriers, support needs) and the preliminary direction of the items. The two discussed for an hour and clarified the division of work: Zhou Haoran would handle the literature support and scientific quality of the items, while Yu Xiaowen would adjust the wording based on clinical practice.

events.name: Participated in the difficult-case discussion in the rehabilitation department.

Yu Xiaowen, drawing on recent literature, proposed an idea of indirectly combining clay hand-shaping training with swallowing muscle stimulation. Although it was still rough, the director encouraged it. The discussion lasted two hours.

events.name: Drafting remarks for the dinner gathering

She drafted several plain and sincere words of thanks and quietly practiced them twice.

Afterwards, she soaked her feet in an electric foot bath with a mugwort pack, listening to classical music while soaking to chase away the chill. She went to bed at 10:30.

She and Wang Fang walked together to a Chinese restaurant in Zhongyuan Wanda Plaza, about 1.5 kilometers away. On the way, they talked about next week's shift schedule and their impressions of their rotations, wrapping their down jackets tightly in the cold wind but laughing continuously.

events.name: Department dinner and annual commendation
events.description: At 7 p.m., over twenty people from the department gathered in a private room at a restaurant for dinner. The dishes were abundant, and everyone chatted while eating in a lively atmosphere. Around 8 o’clock, Director Zhang Lei stood up and announced that the “Annual Research Rising Star” award went to Yu Xiaowen, praising her outstanding performance in this year’s paper publications and clinical data research. Yu Xiaowen stepped forward to receive the award. In her speech, she sincerely thanked her mentor Li Wei for his careful guidance, her colleague Liu Qiang for his collaboration in data analysis, Head Nurse Wu Min for her coordination in patient management, her friend Wang Fang for her emotional support, and Director Zhang for his overall leadership, and said she would continue to work hard. Her colleagues applauded warmly.

events.name: Won an air fryer in the raffle.
events.description: After the commendation came the lucky draw. In the second round, Yu Xiaowen won the second prize: a branded air fryer. Surprised and delighted, she went on stage to receive the award. From below, Wang Fang called out with a laugh, "Next year we can eat the healthy fried chicken you make!" The atmosphere reached a high point. She happily carried the box back to her seat, and everyone crowded around to look.

events.name: After the dinner gathering, walked home and called Father
events.description: At 9:30 the dinner gathering ended. Yu Xiaowen walked back to her residence with Wang Fang, chatting and laughing along the way while carrying the air fryer. At 10 o'clock she got home, put the air fryer in the living room, and immediately made a WeChat video call to her father Yu Jianguo to show off the prize and tell him funny stories from the dinner. Her father said cheerfully in the video, 'Perfect! Come back for the New Year and show me your cooking skills!' The father and daughter agreed to use the air fryer to make low-oil dishes during the New Year. The call lasted about 20 minutes, and her father was also happy that she had won the award. Afterward she washed up and went to sleep at 11.

2025-12.daily_overview: In the early morning, she achieved a 5 km morning run breakthrough. During the day, she summarized her diet and arranged a follow-up appointment. After a short afternoon nap, she prepared items for the night shift and read medical vocabulary. In the evening, while on the night shift, she received an encouraging phone call from her father and officially formulated a New Year study plan for rehabilitation medicine.

events.name: Early morning 5 km run breakthrough
events.description: At 5:30 in the morning, Yu Xiaowen changed into her workout clothes at home, drank a glass of warm water, and warmed up. At 6:00 she arrived at Dongfengqu Riverside Park and started a 5 km morning run along the river path. Under the winter sun, she maintained a pace of 6:24/km and breathed steadily throughout, finishing in 32 minutes, achieving a personal breakthrough in long-distance running. After the run, she stretched on a bench, deeply feeling the satisfaction brought by consistent exercise. Back home, she opened the fitness app to record the data and saw the accumulation of morning runs for the third consecutive week, a good start to her exercise routine for the new year.

events.name: Evaluation of home dietary adjustment effects and decision on follow-up
events.description: After her morning run, she went home to take a shower and eat breakfast (oatmeal porridge + eggs + oranges). In the morning, Yu Xiaowen sat at her desk and compared her compiled food diary and physical change records to evaluate the effect of correcting anemia over the past two months through dietary supplements plus iron supplements: dizziness and fatigue had disappeared, and her complexion was rosy, but she still occasionally felt slightly tired. After weighing things, she decided to go to the hospital's laboratory department the next day for a complete blood count to confirm the indicators.

events.name: Afternoon nap and pre-night-shift preparation.
events.description: From 1 p.m. to 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowen took a one-hour nap in the bedroom to regain energy. After waking up, she packed the items needed for the night shift: a thermos, Jin Jun Mei tea bags, a medical English vocabulary booklet, and a power bank, and synced the notes from her exam prep app on her phone to her tablet. Then she read medical English vocabulary at her desk for 15 minutes, preparing to study in spare moments during the night shift.

events.name: Prepare for the night shift and organize belongings
events.description: After a short rest, Yu Xiaowen put the instruction manual for the newly bought air fryer into the drawer, planning to study it when she had time. She checked her night-shift backpack again to make sure nothing was left behind.

events.name: Received a call from her father during the night shift and made a New Year study plan
events.description: While on the night shift, after finishing ward duties around 9 pm, her father Yu Jianguo called and asked about her career development, shared his experience of continuous learning when he was young, and encouraged her to keep improving. Yu Xiaowen was deeply moved and decided to make preparation for the senior professional title evaluation a key focus for the year and to systematically study cutting-edge advances in rehabilitation medicine. After hanging up, she used her phone in the night shift room to organize professional literature and online course resources on rehabilitation medicine, and in her phone memo she planned a new year study schedule: starting from January 2026, get up one hour earlier every day (from 6:00) to study new theories and research methods in rehabilitation medicine, dividing topics by week, and she set alarm reminders. She planned to spend the first three months completing the first round of systematic review.

start_state.mood: Woke up clear-headed and determined to exercise.

end_state.location: Hospital duty room
end_state.mood: Clear goals, full of fighting spirit for future study.

2025-12.daily_overview: After finishing the night shift, she bought books for exam preparation and had a follow-up blood test confirming that her anemia had been corrected. In the evening, she enjoyed a birthday surprise party carefully prepared by her mother and close friends at home. Late at night, she wrote her annual reflections and achieved self-acceptance.

events.name: Catching up on sleep after the night shift and buying exam prep books
events.description: After getting off the night shift at the hospital and returning home a little after 8 a.m., Yu Xiaowen napped until 11. After waking, she compared the syllabus for the attending physician qualification exam online, ordered “Key Points for the Attending Physician Qualification Exam in Internal Medicine” and “Neurology Review Notes” on JD.com, and sorted her university textbooks into desk drawers by subject.

events.name: Follow-up routine blood test at the hospital laboratory.
events.description: At 2 p.m., Yu Xiaowen went to the Laboratory Department of Zhengzhou Central Hospital, got a complete blood count test order, and had blood drawn. An hour later she received the report: hemoglobin rose to 125 g/L, ferritin was normal, and the anemia had been completely corrected. She happily took a photo of the lab report and saved it to her health records, noting, "Diet adjustment plus iron supplements are effective; iron supplements can be stopped later, maintain the diet."

events.name: Mother and her close friends secretly arranged a birthday party.
events.description: In the afternoon, her mother Li Xiuying set out from home in Zhengzhou and met up with Yu Xiaowen's best friends Zhang Jing, Sun Yue, Wang Fang, Lin Wei, and Su Ya, then secretly decorated Yu Xiaowen's home. Li Xiuying cooked hulatang and longevity noodles in the kitchen; Zhang Jing decorated the living room; Sun Yue prepared to play Mozart's Serenade; Wang Fang placed the wrapped pottery tool gift box on the coffee table; Lin Wei and Su Ya neatly arranged the custom-made pottery knife co-gifted by Zheng Guodong along with the other gifts. Everyone chatted quietly, waiting for her return.

events.name: Surprise birthday party and being moved to tears
events.description: At nearly 6 p.m., Yu Xiaowen arrived home. The moment she turned on the lights, she was pleasantly surprised by the decorations before her and the cheers of everyone. Sun Yue played music, candles lit up, and her mother brought out longevity noodles. Wang Fang gave her a set of professional pottery tools; Zhang Jing gave a deluxe zodiac commemorative coin album; Sun Yue gave a medical English dictionary; Lin Wei gave a badminton racket pendant; and the custom pottery rib tool from Su Ya and Zheng Guodong was handed over by Su Ya. Yu Xiaowen was moved to tears and hugged each friend and her mother, thanking them for their thoughtfulness. Everyone chatted while eating noodles, the atmosphere was warm, and the party lasted two hours.

events.name: Receiving blessings from afar
events.description: During the party, Yu Xiaowen received a birthday blessing video and an electronic card sent from Shenzhen by her high school classmate Liu Yang. She smiled, replied with thanks, and brought up fun memories from high school. Her older brother Yu Xiaofeng also sent a big red envelope and a message via WeChat, saying he would come home early for the Spring Festival.

events.name: Writing year-end reflections late at night
events.description: At 11:00 PM, the party broke up, and her mother and close friends left. Yu Xiaowen sat alone at her desk, opened her diary, and slowly wrote down nearly 200 characters of reflection. She reviewed the past year accompanied by clay, her thesis, her father standing up, her mother's small plates, Bach's melodies, and candlelight, and came to the realization that 'in the spinning of the potter's wheel, she touched a peace resembling eternity.' She summarized that her finances had grown steadily; in family, her father had recovered and her mother was often by her side; in career, her paper had been published and received recognition. In the end, she accepted herself and resolved to guard the fire within her. After writing, she closed the diary, washed up, and fell asleep peacefully.

end_state.mood: Moved, fulfilled, deep self-reconciliation

2025-12.daily_overview: Using annual leave and compensatory time off, the whole family traveled from Zhengzhou back to the old house in Luoyang to be reunited with her parents. In the morning they did Baduanjin in the small courtyard of her parents' home. Her mother cooked hometown dishes, and her father showed off his rehabilitation progress and encouraged her to focus on the attending physician exam. The family rift dissolved, and they welcomed reconciliation and the new year in warmth.

events.name: Morning Baduanjin (at the old house in Luoyang)
events.description: After getting up at 7:30 in the old house in Luoyang, Yu Xiaowen practiced a set of Baduanjin in the living room. Her father sat nearby watching and said he should get some exercise too.

events.name: The whole family returned to the old home in Luoyang
events.description: At 9 AM, Yu Xiaowen drove to pick up her parents at their home in Zhengzhou, and the three of them drove together to the old family home in Luoyang. They traveled along the Lianhuo Expressway for about 2 hours and arrived at No. 42 Kaixuan Road, Xigong District, Luoyang at 11 AM. After arriving, her mother Li Xiuying went into the kitchen and started cooking, while her father Yu Jianguo looked around the old house with his cane, remarking on the changes.

events.name: Mother and daughter prepared a hearty dinner together.
events.description: Yu Xiaowen put down her luggage and went straight into the kitchen to help her mother. The mother and daughter chatted as they washed and cut vegetables. Her mother had prepared her daughter's favorites: hulatang soup, huimian noodles, sweet-and-sour pork, and fruit salad. Yu Xiaowen tried to knead the dough, but her mother laughingly took over, and the kitchen was filled with the aroma of food and laughter.

events.name: Family dinner and father's rehabilitation demonstration
events.description: At 6 p.m., the whole family sat around the dinner table. After dinner, her father, Yu Jianguo, suddenly put down his crutch and slowly walked a few steps independently. Although slow, he was steady, showing great rehabilitation progress. He said to Yu Xiaowen, "Next year, you take the attending physician exam. Dad can walk on his own now — you should live for yourself." Her mother wiped tears from her eyes at the side. Her elder brother, Yu Xiaofeng, joined through a video call and said their sister had worked hard this year, and next year he would come home more often. The atmosphere was warm, and the pressure that had accumulated between generations over the years dissolved the moment her father stood up.

events.name: After-dinner small talk and New Year outlook
events.description: After dinner, the family moved to the living room. Mother cut fruit, father sat on the sofa and video-chatted with older brother about Spring Festival plans, and Yu Xiaowen helped mother tidy the kitchen. She then helped mother clear the dishes while chatting about New Year's Day plans. They decided to help mother with a thorough cleaning during the day on the 31st, then drive back to Zhengzhou in the evening because she is on duty on January 1. Father reminded her to drive carefully and to work hard in the new year. The whole family welcomed the new year with ease.

start_state.mood: Eager to return home, looking forward to reuniting with my parents.

end_state.location: Luoyang old family house
end_state.mood: Warm and relieved, with unprecedented family solidarity.

Her mother gave her a bag of cured meat and sausage to take back to Zhengzhou. After lunch, her father stood at the door to see her off and again urged, 'Drive slowly and do well on the attending physician exam.' At 1 p.m. she drove back to Zhengzhou and arrived home at 3:30.

events.description: Back at home in Zhengzhou, Yu Xiaowen put the cured meat in the refrigerator, checked that the air fryer packaging was intact, and then took a short nap. She woke up at 5, ate a simple bowl of noodles, and prepared her items for the night shift.

events.name: In the evening, jogged 3 kilometers along the Jinshui River.
events.description: Because I was in Luoyang this morning, the morning run could not be done, so I switched to a 3 km jog along the Jinshui River at 6 p.m. to maintain the exercise habit, with a pace of 7 minutes 15 seconds per kilometer. After the run, I went home and took a quick shower.

events.name: Video-calling her parents to ring in the New Year before the last night shift of the year
events.description: Her night shift started at 7 p.m. Before she left for the hospital, her mother proactively sent a video call invitation. On the other side of the screen, her parents were sitting in the living room of their home in Luoyang; her father smiled and said an early Happy New Year. Yu Xiaowen stood her phone on the table to show the tea she had brewed, and the three of them exchanged blessings. Her mother showed her the New Year's extra meal she had prepared for her daughter—dumplings wrapped and placed in the fridge—and said with a smile, "Waiting for you to come back and eat them." Yu Xiaowen reported today's exercise and tomorrow's duty schedule. Her mother reminded her to be safe, and her father said, "We'll meet tomorrow, don't miss us too much." The call lasted about 20 minutes, warm and relaxed. Yu Xiaowen left for the hospital on time.

events.name: Wrote New Year goals during the night shift.
events.description: During a break in the night shift, Yu Xiaowen took out her diary in the duty room and solemnly wrote down three major goals for 2026: 1. Pass the attending physician qualification exam on the first attempt; 2. Continue advancing rehabilitation art research and strive to publish relevant papers; 3. Exercise at least three times a week and maintain a healthy weight. She stuck the note with the goals on the back of her phone case. After writing, she rested in the duty room at 22:30 to build up energy for the early morning ward rounds.

events.name: Went to bed early as planned.
events.description: The night shift was relatively calm. Following the recently adjusted schedule, she rested in the on-call room at 10:30 PM, preparing to take over the ward rounds at 2 AM to ensure a complete sleep cycle.

2025-10.daily_overview: Early this morning, I checked my physical exam report on my phone and found low hemoglobin. Recalling the frequent dizziness and fatigue I'd been having recently, I realized I might be anemic. In the morning, I urgently contacted nutritionist Li Ting to ask about dietary adjustments, carefully writing down her detailed suggestions. In the afternoon, I attended a multidisciplinary consultation organized by the neurology department, proposed a rehabilitation plan based on the functional electrical stimulation knowledge I had prepared, and it was well received. In the evening, I sorted out my consultation notes and reflected on the experience of multidisciplinary collaboration. At night, worried about my health, I searched online for iron-rich recipes and called my mother to update her. Although I felt a little anxious about my health during the day, my professional performance at work brought a strong sense of accomplishment.

events.name: View the electronic physical examination report
events.description: At 6:50 a.m., while preparing breakfast in the kitchen, Yu Xiaowen logged into the hospital app on her phone and checked the electronic report of the previous day's physical examination. She noticed that her hemoglobin in the complete blood count was only 105 g/L, below the normal range, suggesting mild iron-deficiency anemia. She immediately took screenshots of the key indicators and wrote them down in her memo, planning to consult a professional.

events.name: Recall recent physical symptoms and perform a preliminary self-check.
events.description: After seeing the anemia results, Yu Xiaowen recalled the dizziness and fatigue she often felt after work in recent months. Previously, while in the internal medicine department, she had always assumed it was due to shift work and lack of sleep, but after transferring departments, she still had occasional episodes despite a regular schedule. Only then did she realize there might be another cause. She quickly reviewed her daily diet in her mind, suspected she wasn't eating enough meat, and decided to look up nutrition information after work.

events.name: Contact a colleague in the nutrition department to schedule a consultation.
events.description: At 8:10 in the morning, after Yu Xiaowen arrived at the hospital, she sent a message to Li Ting, a colleague in the nutrition department, via the internal messaging software, briefly explaining the abnormal physical examination results and hoping to consult in person about dietary adjustments. Li Ting replied quickly and agreed to meet at the nutrition department office at 10 o'clock.

events.name: Go to the Department of Nutrition for a detailed consultation
events.description: At 10:00 AM, Yu Xiaowen arrived at the nutrition department office on time. She described her low hemoglobin level and recent symptoms in detail to Li Ting. Li Ting advised her to increase her intake of red meat (100-150 grams per day), pork liver (once or twice a week, 50 grams each time), and dark-colored vegetables, while also giving up coffee and strong tea and switching to fruit tea rich in vitamin C to promote iron absorption. Yu Xiaowen carefully wrote down every suggestion.

events.name: Organize key points for dietary adjustments
events.description: After the consultation ended and she returned to the rehabilitation department office, Yu Xiaowen sat at her workstation and organized Li Ting's suggestions item by item into her personal health management notebook, including food types, recommended portions, eating frequency, and beverage replacement options, and highlighted the precautions in red pen.

events.name: Preparing for multidisciplinary consultation
events.description: At 2:00 p.m., using the fragmented time after her lunch break, Yu Xiaowen reviewed the electronic medical records and imaging reports of complex stroke patients on the office computer, reviewed recent literature on functional electrical stimulation, and organized the key points of a possible neuromuscular electrical stimulation plan.

events.name: Participated in the neurology multidisciplinary consultation
events.description: At 3:00 p.m., Yu Xiaowen went to the neurology department conference room to discuss the case with the chief physician, rehabilitation therapist, and nutritionist. With her rehabilitation perspective, she suggested adding neuromuscular electrical stimulation to the regular exercise training and explained the clinical rationale. Her suggestion was recognized by the experts and included in the final rehabilitation plan.

events.name: Organizing consultation notes and reflections.
events.description: After the consultation ended at 5:30 p.m., Yu Xiaowen returned to the office and organized the opinions of various departments and the final comprehensive rehabilitation pathway into structured notes. She wrote down her takeaways in her personal work journal, especially deepening her understanding of the role of multidisciplinary collaboration in rehabilitation.

events.name: Searched online for iron-rich recipes and contacted her mother
events.description: At 9:00 p.m., Yu Xiaowen sat on the living room sofa, opened her laptop, and searched for iron-supplementing recipes for anemia. She saved several recipes for spinach and pork liver congee and beef hulatang. Then she made a video call to her mother in Luoyang, told her that her physical exam showed mild anemia and she was adjusting her diet. Her mother urged her to eat more red dates and pork liver, and taught her a simple hulatang recipe.
